To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron-electron interactions in the leads of open quantum dots can have profound effects on transport properties.

the electron-electron interactions lead to the pinning of the energy levels in the quantum dot in the presence of external perturbation, and that the pinning becomes more pronounced with increasing magnetic field.

the screening in open quantum dots is much more efficient than that in closed quantum dots, that the resonant energy level pinning to the Fermi level occurs in open dots, that this pinning effect becomes stronger with increasing magnetic field, and that these findings can have a profound impact on transport properties of open systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of electron-electron interactions on the electronic transport through open systems, such as quantum dots, and its implications for the edge state transport.
the study of the role of electron-electtron interaction in the transport properties of open systems.
the study of the effect of electron-electron interactions on transport properties of open systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron-electron interactions play a crucial role in the transport properties of the open quantum dots.
a proper treatment of the electron-electron interactions in open systems leads to significant qualitative changes in the transport properties of quantum dots.
the pinning of the energy levels is a general property of open quantum systems and is independent of the specific model used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron-electron correlation effects can be significant even for the open system and that the self-consistent calculations are required to obtain a reliable description.
the electron-electron interactions in quantum dots are important and cannot be ignored.
the electron-electron interactions play a crucial role in the magnetotransport of open quantum dots.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electron-electron interactions in open quantum systems are not a small perturbation, and should be treated on the same level as the external fields (i.e. magnetic field, electrostatic potential, etc.).
the effect of the pinning of resonances is very sensitive to the electron-electron screening.
the pinning effect can be observed in the transport properties of open dots only if the electron-electron interactions are accounted for both in semi-infinitive lead as well as in a dot region.
